changelog: Shared craft-common base: new optional argBase64Keys, jsonTextKeys and previewTools options (for DesignCraft); no change in this plugin's tools.
name: GridCraft
description: Headless spreadsheet (GridCraft from ArtCraft, open source, written in Rust). Formulas, tables, sorting and filtering, pivot tables and charts; opens XLSX, ODS and CSV; saves XLSX and CSV and exports PDF.
instructions:
GridCraft runs headless in your own container; every file lives in /work.

1. Upload the user's spreadsheet (.xlsx, .ods, .csv) to /work and open it: open_workbook {"path":"/work/data.csv"} (a CSV opens as one sheet named after the file). Or start an empty one with new_workbook {}.
2. Look at the data first: inspect_workbook {} shows the sheets, used ranges, tables and charts; read_range {"range":"A1:D20"} returns the values ("Sheet2!A1:B3" for another sheet). Enter values and formulas with write_range or set_cell (text starting with = is a formula), try a formula with evaluate_formula.
3. Pivot table and chart: execute_command {"command":"insert.pivotTable","params":{"rows":["Region"],"columns":["Product"],"values":[{"field":"Sales","func":"sum"}]}} builds it on a new sheet from the data around the selection and answers its sheet and range; then execute_command {"command":"insert.pivotChart","params":{"type":"column","title":"Sales by region"}}. For a chart of plain data use insert_chart {"range":"A1:B10","type":"column","title":"..."}. create_table, sort_range, filter and format_range cover the common rest.
4. Everything else (conditional formatting, number formats, data validation, find and replace, remove duplicates…) is an engine command: list_commands {"search":"duplicate"} — the argument is search, always pass one, never list all — then execute_command {"command":...,"params":{...}}. list_functions {"search":"lookup"} lists worksheet functions.
5. Save always with a path in /work, using new file names, never overwriting the user's input: save_workbook {"path":"/work/result.xlsx"} (all sheets, pivot tables and charts); save_workbook {"path":"/work/result.csv"} writes the active sheet only (switch with select {"range":"Sheet1!A1"}); PDF with execute_command {"command":"file.exportPdf","params":{"path":"/work/result.pdf","sheets":"all"}}.
6. Hand the result over: download it from /work with plugin_download_file.

All paths must be inside /work; relative paths resolve against /work. Any text argument that starts with / or ../ (also a cell value in write_range or set_cell) is checked as a file path and refused when it points outside /work, so rephrase such text; formulas such as =A1/B1 start with = and are fine. File bytes are never returned inline: file.saveBytes is refused, save with save_workbook and a path instead. A new MCP session (e.g. after a reconnect) starts with no open workbook, so save an .xlsx after each stage and reopen it then. The container and /work are deleted after the conversation is idle, so always download the results.

accepts.description: Excel workbook to analyse or edit
OpenDocument spreadsheet to analyse or edit

returns.description: Saved Excel workbook with pivot tables and charts
